item.title: ‘Jalen Brunson wants…’ – Ex-WNBA star details why New York Knicks are struggling this season
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Former WNBA player Chiney Ogwumike names the biggest problem for the New York Knicks. After the New York Knicks won the 2026 NBA Championship, fans expected a solid showing from the franchise in the 2026-27 season as well. However, this season hasn’t been kind to the Knicks, as they are currently the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 9-6 record. As a result, fans are already starting to lose hope for a potential back-to-back NBA Championship run from the team. But what’s the reason behind the Knicks’ early-season struggles? Chiney Ogwumike says the New York Knicks need to change their ‘recipe’ Last season, the Knicks took teams by surprise with their tactics under head coach Mike Brown. Brown’s approach has remained relatively unchanged this season as well. According to former WNBA star Chiney Ogwumike, that’s where the problem lies for the defending NBA champions. “There’s no surprise factor anymore. Like everyone knows that this is a team that can beat anybody, the scouting report’s out, Jalen Brunson wants to close games and I think that you can’t use the same recipe and expect different results. The rest of the Eastern Conference is different. You sort of have to tweak some things,” Ogwumike began. “Now, I know it’s probably going to be sensitive with that starting lineup, but I would give them a little bit more time to sort of ease themselves into that possibility,” she further stated. In simple terms, the ESPN analyst wants coach Brown to experiment with different lineups and tactics, instead of relying on what worked last season. To be fair, the Knicks won the NBA title with those exact tactics, but the off-season has allowed other teams to be well-prepared for them, and the team’s 9-6 record is a perfect reflection of it. item.title: Bob Chesney reveals main message to UCLA amid CFP push
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Bob Chesney reveals main message to UCLA amid CFP push appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UCLA football Bruins have not been named a national champion since 1954. They have never won 11 games in a single campaign. They won just eight games combined across the previous two seasons. A 10-0 record carries significant weight for alumni, and top-four standing in the Playoff rankings carries even more. This program has completely transformed under Bob Chesney . But the head coach does not care about what the success represents, at least not right now. He is more concerned about how that success is achieved. Ahead of Saturday’s road game versus Michigan , Chesney is stressing the importance of ignoring all the outside praise. Hunger is fueled by a lack of satisfaction. He wants his players to be starving when they brave a rowdy Ann Arbor crowd that has nothing to celebrate except for a potential upset win versus a national title contender. “I said it back when we first got ranked. ‘Look, there’s a little number next to your name right now, and if you want to pay attention to that number, it will very quickly disappear. If you want to pay attention to how you got the number, and the process in which you did to earn that number, then who knows, maybe it could get a little bit better,'” the 2025 Sun Belt Coach of the Year (James Madison) said on SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “After every single game, I walk in on Sunday morning and just say it doesn’t matter. Get better. Period. You had a bad play? It doesn’t matter. Get better. The next play is about to happen whether you like it or not. The next game is about to happen whether you like it or not, and you can’t let a previous success or failure determine our next success or failure.” Did you run through a brick wall yet? "We can't hold back and let a previous success or failure determine our next success or failure." UCLA head coach Bob Chesney joins @notthefakeSVP ahead of their game against Michigan and speaks on the message to his team 🏈 pic.twitter.com/he9W0NDtl9 — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 21, 2026 Bob Chesney obviously has his players focused on the right things. UCLA football is rising at a meteoric pace , but it will instantly cool off with one loss versus a .500 Michigan squad. Keeping a locker room from getting too high or too low is an essential part of the job. And this man is clearly up to the task. The Bruins can reach that perpetually elusive 11th win, but they will hear Chesney’s “it doesn’t matter speech” if and when they reach that milestone. However, the school and fan base will certainly bask in that historic moment. UCLA-Michigan kicks off at about 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday. item.title: “He is Such a Hypocrite”: Fans Torch Nick Saban as He Seemingly Changes Tack on Lane Kiffin’s Move to LSU from Ole Miss
item.description: Lane Kiffin and Nick Saban © Imagn Nick Saban was all for giving head coaches their due and supported Lane Kiffin when the former Ole Miss boss decided to head to LSU, but he has seemingly changed course after some poor performances this season for the Tigers. The former Alabama coach said that had Kiffin stayed at Ole Miss, he would have been able to build the team around Trinidad Chambliss. “I think if Lane Kiffin stayed at Ole Miss, they would have been able to build that team around Trinidad Chambliss…I respect Sam Leavitt as a competitor, and he makes a lot of plays…If you could just eliminate his bad plays, LSU would be in a completely different position,” Saban said on the Pat McAfee Show. Fans reacted to Saban’s comments, with one fan saying, “But Saban is the voice that was in Lane’s ear to leave Ole Miss for LSU. He is such a hypocrite. Saban can’t even give Pete Golding an ounce of credit.” Lane Kiffin Spoke About Returning to Tennessee As LSU prepares to play Tennessee on Saturday, Lane Kiffin was asked how it feels to play against his former team. Kiffin referred to the emotionally charged game against Ole Miss this season, when fans turned out in huge numbers to watch him return to his old stomping grounds. “I’m not challenging Tennessee, but I just don’t think you can top that (the atmosphere at Ole Miss),” Kiffin said , per USA Today. “Just the feeling of what that was like, and the anger and hatred, because it was so recent.” Kiffin coached Tennessee in 2009 and went 7-6 with the Vols before leaving to become head coach at USC. item.title: “This Claim Is Absolutely Delusional”: Fans Push Back as Tim Tebow Calls LSU “The Most Dangerous Team in the Country” Ahead of Tennessee Clash
item.description: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect LSU is unranked and coming off back-to-back losses, but former Florida quarterback Tim Tebow believes they are still one of the most dangerous teams in college football. The Tigers enter Saturday’s game against No. 9 Tennessee at 6-4 after a 22-21 defeat to Texas last week. Speaking on ESPN, Tebow showed extreme confidence in LSU, despite its recent struggles. “I think they’re the most dangerous team in the country. They’re unranked and maybe one of the top three or four most talented teams in the country,” Tebow said. Tebow’s assessment did not convince many fans on social media. They’re going to go to some bowl game they don’t want to go to. You’ve got a head coach that may be called out part of his roster. So that’s one concern,” he said on The Triple Option podcast. “The best version of LSU, we said this about four weeks ago, could compete and win it all. I don’t think we’re going to see the best version again.” With Tennessee looking to protect its playoff hopes and LSU attempting to finish its season strongly, Saturday’s game promises to be a thriller. item.title: “He Tried to Trade for Him”: NFL Fans React After John Harbaugh’s Viral Response to Colts Cutting QB Daniel Jones
item.description: John Harbaugh © Reuters Connect The Indianapolis Colts have waived quarterback Daniel Jones after an unimpressive performance against the Houston Texans on Thursday night, and it appears the news hit John Harbaugh like a ton of bricks. The New York Giants head coach was asked about Jones at his press conference and appeared stunned, sparking wild reactions on social media. One fan said “he tried to trade for him”, while others wondered whether it might have been an act by Harbaugh. “He tried to trade for him,” the fan wrote. Head Coach Shane Steichen’s Statement on the Colts Cutting Daniel Jones Colts head coach Shane Steichen appreciated Daniel Jones after the franchise waived the QB, expressing his positivity in an official statement. “Can’t say enough good things about Daniel, just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate, the toughness that he brought to our football team. Can’t say enough good things about him,” Steichen said, per the NFL website . “I mean, the guy played on a broken leg for us last year for three or four games, snaps his Achilles, came back in eight and a half months, and gave this organization everything he had. Couldn’t be more thankful for the time I had with him.” Jones completed just 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and one interception on Thursday night, and the writing was on the wall as Anthony Richardson replaced the QB in the final minutes. The Colts play the Giants on Sunday, 29 Nov. in their next NFL game. item.title: Steven Fakult leads Nordonia into OHSAA football state semifinal
item.description: TWINSBURG – The Nordonia football team completed its "Revenge Tour" on Friday, Nov. 20, in dramatic fashion. Senior quarterback Steven Fakult threw five touchdown passes, including one in overtime to senior Dominick Jackson in Nordonia's 35-28 win over Highland in the Division II, Region 5 championship at Twinsburg Tiger Stadium. “That’s what we practice,” Jackson said of the game-winning TD. “We have run that play a thousand times through my 10 years playing football here. So, we just had to put the emotion down and just do what we do best and just go make a play. … Steven is one my best buds. He's the greatest guy. People [at colleges] need to start taking more looks at him. He makes plays. He wins games.” Nordonia (12-1) advanced to play Columbus Bishop Watterson (12-0) in a state semifinal at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 27, at a site to be determined by the OHSAA. Nordonia is a state semifinalist for the first time since 2014 when it finished as Division II state runners-up. The Knights were also Division II state runners-up in 2002 and Division II state semifinalists in 2006. Watterson, the Division III state champion in 2024 and 2025, isn't part of the "Revenge Tour," but Highland (11-2) was. Nordonia’s path to a state semifinal included wins over the five teams that defeated the Knights since the start of last season. “You don't really get that many opportunities in high school football, so when you go out there you have to make the most of it, and we are fired up,” Jackson said. North Royalton, Wadsworth and Hudson beat Nordonia in the regular season in 2025, and Walsh Jesuit eliminated the Knights in a regional quarterfinal playoff game last season. Nordonia defeated Hudson, North Royalton and Wadsworth in the regular season in 2026, and eliminated Walsh Jesuit in a regional semifinal. Highland topped Nordonia 23-21 on Sept. 11 before the Knights reversed that outcome Friday in the postseason. “It all starts in the offseason,” Nordonia senior linebacker-running back-wide receiver Karsen Fisher said. “… So, this offseason it was all forget that — we are going to go beat your butt during this season, and we did that. Hudson and Wadsworth were the big ones. I had never beaten either of them until this season. "It was my personal duty to beat everybody we lost to. I made sure to keep the energy at practice, and this week especially with Highland. This is a regional freaking championship, man.” Jackson caught two of Fakult’s TD passes — a 35-yard strike in the second quarter and a 17-yard strike in overtime. Fakult threw a 27-yard TD pass to senior Grant Kaminski on a 4th-and-10 and a 5-yard TD pass to junior Jamison Elerick in the third quarter and a 1-yard TD pass to senior CJ Mayes on 4th-and-goal play. “We saw a cover 2, cover 4 type of defense, which is really kind of unorthodox for them,” Fakult said of the final TD pass to Jackson. “Usually it's been cover 3, cover 1. item.title: Skip Bayless names ‘the best player’ in the NFL right now
item.description: Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Skip Bayless has called Josh Allen the best player in the NFL while speaking about why he should be the MVP ahead of Joe Burrow. Allen previously won the award in 2024 and is in the midst of another impressive season with his Buffalo Bills 8-1 ahead of their Week 11 game. The Bills quarterback has some strong competition for the award this year, including from Joe Burrow. But while Bayless thinks the Cincinnati Bengals star is ‘the ultimate system quarterback’, he is of the opinion that ‘Allen has revolutionised’ the QB role and is ‘the best player in football and he should be the MVP’. Speaking on First Take, he said: “Josh Allen has revolutionised the quarterback position in ways I never thought I would see in my lifetime because he has scored 11 rushing touchdowns in the red zone. He’s become the Derrick Henry of quarterbacks. He is just simply unstoppable. “While Joe Burrow is the ultimate system quarterback, almost always throwing it on time, Josh Allen’s offence is mostly backyard. I think he makes up almost every play. He’s getting away with a running back who weighs 190 pounds running between the tackles. “It is all Josh Allen. He’s the best player in football and he should be the MVP.” How Josh Allen and Joe Burrow compare Allen currently has a better record with the Bills this season but Burrow does lead him in some key stats. The Bengals quarterback has the second-most passing yards in the NFL (2,795), which is considerably more than Josh (2,223). He also has a much higher completion rate (74.7%) compared to Allen (65.0%) and has more passing yards per game (310.6 vs 247.0). But as Bayless suggested, the Bills player is a pretty unique style of quarterback as he actually leads the league in rushing touchdowns (11) alongside Jahmyr Gibbs. Burrow is the joint-closest quarterback to matching Allen on that front but he only has three rushing touchdowns. It remains to be seen who will be crowned MVP this season but both players should still be in contention, and while Skip may be supporting Allen’s claim, others disagree. Among them is Tom Brady, who says it’s ‘pretty obvious’ Burrow is the best quarterback in the league. item.title: “Spoken Like a Man Who May Want a Job One Day”: Fans Aren’t Convinced as Former Colts Star Defends Carlie Irsay-Gordon Amid Criticism of Her Leadership
item.description: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon walks on the field before the game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. © Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Carlie Irsay-Gordon has come under increasing scrutiny as the Indianapolis Colts continue to struggle through a disappointing season. Following the team’s embarrassing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, fans and several analysts shared their disappointment with the owner. However, former Colts star Stephon Gilmore has pushed back against those criticisms, expressing confidence in Irsay-Gordon’s leadership. Gilmore defended the Colts owner on social media, saying he has personally seen her involved in team meetings and believes she understands football better than many give her credit for. “Yall have to chill on Carlie Irsay. I’ve seen her in meetings. She knows more ball than a lot of so-called football people. She’s very passionate about the game and the Colts. I’ve seen her in meetings. She will get the @Colts right in due time. Watch,” he wrote. However, Gilmore’s defense did not convince everyone, and several fans questioned his comments and the Colts’ recent decisions. One fan wrote, “Spoken like a man who may want a job one day down the road.” “Rejecting trade offers for Daniel Jones only to release him right after the deadline must be some kind of 4D chess I don’t understand,” another wrote. “Look man she needs to have taken the picks she dropped the ball on this one and she HAS GOT to wear the blame,” one fan wrote. “Some 4D chess there, not trading DJ before the deadline,” another wrote. “Good for her, but any owner who thinks their presence on the sideline isn’t a distraction is a problem. Regardless if they are male or female,” another added. Analyst Blames Carlie Irsay-Gordon for Colts’ Collapse NFL analyst Michael Holley delivered a harsh assessment of Irsay-Gordon’s leadership on Pro Football Talk after the Houston loss. “This is gonna sound crazy. But their owner ruined their season. We can say how bad they are and that stat and how bad they are and they get a prize for that. They still have three wins. They went into a game last night with the Houston Texans, who also had three wins. So it’s not like we were watching the Jaguars against the Titans. We were watching two three-win teams last night,” Holley said. He argued that the decision to fire general manager Chris Ballard and to trade away several key players derailed Indianapolis’ season. He continued questioning whether the coaching staff could still effectively manage players and end the season on a good note. The Colts have struggled significantly this season; against Houston, they recorded just 167 total yards. With the franchise facing questions about its direction, Irsay-Gordon has very little time to make changes and turn things around to silence the critics. item.description: Celtic v St Mirren – This is the day when Kasper Hogh puts one away Kasper Hogh will be a vital player today, he will be one of the first names on the team sheet, and with good reason… Kasper Hogh of Celtic scores the opening goal only for VAR to rule it out for a foul in the build up during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Kasper Hogh is a player who is under a huge amount of scrutiny at the moment due to his three month run without a goal. The £11 million man hasn’t hit the back of the net since his first half hat trick at Rugby Park at the beginning of August, and it’s understandably being used against him due to him being a centre forward, one that the club shelled out a record £11 million for. Kasper Hogh of Celtic is challenged by Emmanuel Agbadou of Besiktas JK during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Despite his goal drought, and the criticism that comes with it, Kasper hasn’t allowed it to get him down, and the Danish international has put in some impressive performances as he shows there’s more to his game than just being a poacher. He was however signed to score goals, and he did find the net once again against Kilmarnock a fortnight ago, only to see it cruelly ruled out by VAR for a foul by Mika Baur in the build up. I have no doubts that Kasper will start today, In fact I’d be willing to place a small wager that he’ll be in the starting XI when the teams are announced later this afternoon. item.title: Missing Newcastle United home matches
item.description: The Mag Pod Jamie Simon Hutch Watching Game St James' Park Newcastle United First off, I need to start with an apology to anyone coming to The Mag to read my report on whatever happens/has happened against Arsenal , I have decided to allow the editor to flex his squad strength due to my not being there today, missing Newcastle United home matches is, for me at least, a difficult business. I can already imagine some reading this are flabbergasted that someone with a ticket for a game against the Premier League champions would allow themselves to be otherwise occupied when they would crawl over broken all sorts to be there at any time. The thing is, I’m a bit of a victim of poor prediction skills, as a look at any of my recent accas will confirm. A few of my close mates were after arranging a meet up and a poll appeared in the WhatsApp group giving a choice of three weekends. One option was next week when I’m in Brighton, another was the untouchable territory of derby weekend and the remaining option was the Gunners at home. I took a punt and committed to this weekend, knowing that if the game was shifted to Sunday (or any other mad weekend kick off that wasn’t Saturday) I’d be able to get to it, convincing myself we’d be the Sunday warm up to Liverpool v Man Utd. So, it came to pass that wasn’t to be. So what do you do? Ditch your old mates and head to the game, or give someone else a chance with your ticket? Again, opinions will be polarised as some commentators will doubtless be about to say that they would chop their hand off with a rusty spoon to be in that ground, whereas many others will have found themselves in the position where they choose life over NUFC. I haven’t made this kind of miscalculation very often, with most of my absences from Newcastle United home matches being early season when it’s clashed with a holiday. Memories of enduring last season’s defeat to Liverpool in a bar at Disneyland Paris with an obnoxious cockney red mouthing off behind me are not amongst my most magical. It’s maybe a bit easier to swallow missing a defeat though. I’ll always remember when my youngest son was born and I confidently thought to myself he’d arrive in plenty of time for me to get to the game with Norwich in about six days. Mrs S saw it quite differently and her reaction to the prospect of me leaving her with a newborn and two toddlers as she recovered from a c-section was, if I’m honest, a bit over the top. I stayed at home and checked online to catch the news of Dwight Gayle’s 96th minute hat-trick goal sealing an incredible 4-3 comeback win. Honestly, during the whole Mike Ashley era it was a bit easier to give things a swerve. I remember hauling myself out of the house on a freezing Wednesday evening full of cold. item.title: Baldini advises Camarda ‘father to son’ and has great expectations for Bartesaghi: ‘A luxury’
item.description: Baldini advises Camarda ‘father to son’ and has great expectations for Bartesaghi: ‘A luxury’ Italy U21s head coach Silvio Baldini says that he has spoken to Francesco Camarda ‘like father-to-son’ and has tipped both Alphadjo Cisse and Davide Bartesaghi to reach the highest heights in the professional game: ‘If I were the coach of any Serie A club, I would take him with me’. Baldini shared his thoughts on Milan’s cohort of young Italian talents in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, published on Saturday. Baldini talks Cisse, Camarda and Bartesaghi: ‘A luxury for the U21s’ The Azzurrini head coach says that he is impressed with the development and maturity that Cisse has shown over the last year. ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Alphadjo Cisse of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) It has been a rapid rise to the top for the Rossoneri winger, who was playing in Serie B with Catanzaro six months ago, has already been fast-tracked through the Italy U21 side and was called up to the senior national side by Roberto Mancini earlier this month. “Compared to a year ago, I see a completely different guy, stronger, more mature and more prepared with a lot more self-esteem,” Baldini told La Gazzetta dello Sport . “He has Milan to thank for taking him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and giving him an opportunity to play consistently. If he moves up to the national team and does well, even better.” Baldini credited Milan with scouting and developing Cisse, but La Gazzetta dello Sport suggested that it is Baldini who discovered that Cisse could be equally as effective through the middle as he is off the wing. A humble Baldini shrugged off those suggestions: “After analysing the training sessions, there were lots of situations where he managed to score by attacking space from depth. item.title: PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle
item.description: PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. With just three points separating the two clubs, the encounter promises to be one of Matchday 10’s most fascinating fixtures. Bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12. Both clubs have enjoyed encouraging spells this season, making the derby particularly significant beyond their historic rivalry. Bremen’s home advantage and Füllkrug’s influence Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break. The Weserstadion has become a major advantage. Bremen remain unbeaten there this season, collecting 10 points from four matches. Niclas Füllkrug has been instrumental in their resurgence, scoring nine Bundesliga goals in nine appearances. Hamburg, meanwhile, have struggled away from home, losing four of their five matches on the road. However, their recent 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach demonstrated their attacking potential, particularly through Miro Muheim’s dangerous long-range shooting. More than just three points The Nordderby also presents an intriguing managerial storyline. Thioune previously coached Hamburg and worked alongside current Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin at Osnabrück before their paths crossed again in Hamburg. History favours Bremen, who have won eight of their previous nine Bundesliga home encounters against their northern rivals. Last season, however, both clubs won their respective home derbies, highlighting the unpredictable nature of this fixture. For Bremen, victory would reinforce their European ambitions and demonstrate that their impressive start is sustainable. Hamburg, meanwhile, have an opportunity to move level on points with their rivals and strengthen their position in the Bundesliga. Regardless of their respective league positions, the Nordderby represents something much bigger than three points. It is a contest shaped by history, regional pride and the desire to establish supremacy in northern Germany. With both teams showing encouraging signs this season, Sunday’s encounter has all the ingredients to deliver another memorable chapter in one of the Bundesliga’s greatest rivalries. GGFN | Felipe

item.title: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play
item.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It’s one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions. Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That’s an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000. Under the new policy, the maximum time allowed for a single shot also drops from 70 seconds to 60 seconds, and players will pay $2,000 for a first offense, $4,000 for a second, and $8,000 for a third. Delays of six to 15 seconds still bring a one-stroke penalty plus a fine, while delays of 16 seconds or more carry a two-stroke penalty and a fine. LPGA Tour Commissioner Craig Kessler explained how the tour came to this new policy. LPGA Tour Commissioner explains new pace of play policy This new pace-of-play policy is a positive step for the LPGA Tour as it looks to speed up the game, and what’s even more encouraging is that the players are also invested in fixing the issue. How do we know that? Well, the players came up with the solution in the first place. That’s according to Kessler, who said on SiriusXM Radio: “The good news is we started with our fans, and the insight from fans is that pace of play matters. Fans want to see us play faster. We brought that to our players, and we actually have a pace-of-play committee. “And the beautiful thing here is it’s the players who developed the policy. They’re the ones that we understand the importance of playing faster. We understand what are the levers that we can pull to help bring that to life. “And they’re the ones who created the policy that we rolled out to frankly, a decent amount of applause from our players on Tuesday. “I’m very excited to see the policy implemented. If it works as intended, fantastic, and of course if we need to learn and adapt as we go then we’ll do just that.” This isn’t the only step the LPGA Tour has taken. Obviously, Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders have no wide receiver room at all. He would be a great No. 1,” McIntyre said. Las Vegas selected Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. item.title: Harden passes Bryant for 50-point games
item.description: Harden joined the Cavaliers in February after three years with the Los Angeles Clippers [Getty Images] James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup. The 37-year-old made all 14 of his free throws as his recorded his 26th 50-point game to move above the legendary Kobe Bryant. Harden, who also made six rebounds and provided six assists at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, had not passed 50 points since scoring 55 for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025. Legendary centre Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record ⁠with 118 50-point games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31. "When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe - shooting guard position, the best to ever do it - so just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," said an emotional Harden. Aged 37 years and 86 days, he is the fourth oldest player to score 50 points in a game. "What excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful," said Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points. "It's easy when you're young - 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast. "That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. "Tonight was a confidence-booster that I can do it at a high level still." The Cavaliers travel to the Chicago Bulls in the NBA on Tuesday.

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their group – but both were beaten in a stunning penultimate round of pool action. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. item.title: Pat Cummins to stay as Australia captain after ‘unanimous support’ amid Sandpapergate row
item.description: Pat Cummins will hold on to his role as Australia captain despite the ongoing pressure of the sandpaper scandal , after receiving a show of “unanimous support” from Cricket Australia. Cummins’ future had become a topic of hot debate following a fortnight of claims and counter claims concerning the ball tampering furore of 2018. His emphatic denials of any awareness of or involvement in the plot, which he shared in a strident 69-minute press conference in Sydney last week, contradicted testimony of several former team-mates and raised questions over the seamer’s leadership. Pat Cummins will continue as Australia captain (Reuters) Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography and an exhaustive written account from Cameron Bancroft alleged that the entire squad, as well as some members of the backroom staff, shared responsibility for Sandpapergate, with backing from former team-mates including David Warner and Chadd Sayers. An independent forum was announced by CA in a bid to collate the experiences of all those involved in the South Africa tour eight years ago but before it has even begun, the governing body has made it clear that it stands firmly alongside Cummins. And while that is unlikely to satisfy everybody – not least Khawaja, who saw his account branded “complete and utter nonsense” by his former skipper – it means Cummins can expect to lead the side again against New Zealand next month and can begin to plan for next summer’s Ashes campaign in England. The claims in Usman Khawaja’s autobiography started the furore (Reuters) A statement issued on Saturday read: “In the light of the ongoing speculation surrounding the Australian men’s team tour of South Africa in 2018, the CA Board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian Cricket and the welfare of all concerned. “As part of this meeting, the board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position.” Both Khawaja and Warner, meanwhile, were late omissions from the Fox television commentary roster having both been lined up to feature. With battle lines drawn, the momentum appears to be moving against them. Cummins, who has seen his previous position as the golden boy of Australian sport challenged by negative headlines and reporters doorstepping him at home and training, said: “It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd on Friday. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly. “David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018. “I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what’s needed. Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority.”

item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
